The five titles that got away as Evans seeks WRC glory
description: As Elfyn Evans looks to finally clinch the World Rally Championship title in Sardinia, BBC Sport looks back at the five times he finished runner-up.
fullText:
Few leading sports stars have been so tantalisingly close to crowning glory for so long without achieving ultimate success as rally driver Elfyn Evans.

The 37-year-old from Dolgellau in north-west Wales has been runner-up in the World Rally Championship (WRC) five times in the past six years.

But that could all be about to change.

With this year's WRC calendar truncated by the removal of the planned Saudi Arabia finale, Evans takes a 17-point lead into the now season-ending Rally Italia Sardegna from 1-4 October.

If Evans can maintain his advantage over team-mates Sami Pajari and Oliver Solberg it will be a crowning moment for the Welshman, who would become only the third Briton to win the WRC title - joining Colin McRae and Richard Burns.

As he prepares to grasp history in Sardinia, BBC Sport looks back at the five times Evans fell just short of his dream.

No change for leader Evans after WRC drops finale

White, Netherlands, Evans and sport's other great runners-up

BBC to broadcast World Rally Championship from 2027

Evans does have a world title - winning the WRC Junior Championship in 2012 which earned him a full-time seat in M-Sport's Ford Fiesta.

However, it was a move to Toyota Gazoo Racing in 2020 that put his senior career into overdrive.

Only huge last-event misfortune cost him instant success in a season cut from 13 races to seven by the Covid-19 pandemic.

After placing third at Monte Carlo in his first Yaris outing, Evans and co-driver Scott Martin excelled at a weather-shortened second round to win Rally Sweden.

It put the Welshman top of the WRC driver's championship for the first time, and although record-breaking Sebastien Ogier would temporarily reclaim the lead, a second victory in Turkey saw Evans take at 14-point advantage over the Frenchman into the final event.

With 10 of the 16 stages complete, the less experienced of the two drivers remained on course for a maiden championship success.

But Evans' dream ended in devastating fashion when he crashed down a bank after being caught out by treacherous snow-covered mountain roads.

Ogier claimed a seventh world title by just eight points to leave his team-mate "gutted".

"When I braked on that, it was just like glass and there was no chance of us slowing down at all. It completely caught me by surprise," said Evans after the race, later admitting "it was a massive disappointment", which made him "more determined" for the year ahead.

Evans took that determination and experience into the new year and soon grabbed the lead in the season-opening Rallye Monte Carlo.

However, local favourite Ogier went on to win in Monaco, and then three more of the first six rounds to take a commanding grip of the 2021 championship.

The Welsh driver was not about to give up though. A second rally win of the season in Finland. and second place in the penultimate round at Rally Catalunya, once again forced the title race into a final-event decider at Monza.

With a potentially bridgeable gap of 17 points, the two Toyota rally crews swapped the lead throughout - but Ogier and co-driver Julien Ingrassia eventually came out on top to claim both the rally and the title.

"It's been a pretty OK year," a typically level-headed Evans reflected at the end of the race.

"Of course, I can't help but feel a little disappointed right now, you always look to the places you could've done better."

The following year could certainly have been much better - as Evans struggled with the newly introduced hybrid cars.

Going off the road in the opening round and forced to retire from three further rallies, Evans finished 2022 in fourth place, more than 120 points behind first-time champion Kalle Rovanpera.

"2022 fell below our expectations," a defiant Evans told the BBC before the 2023 campaign.

"We're coming into the new season looking for improvements - and we're hoping we can challenge for the title."

And challenge he did - winning round four in Croatia to take a share of the championship lead, tied with Ogier and one point ahead of Rovanperra.

However, a crash at Rally Portugal set his title bid back as he was forced to retire in round five and - despite a victory in Finland - Evans had to concede the title with one round to go.

A crash and a disappointing finish at the Central European Rally may have handed back-to-back titles to Finnish team-mate Rovanpera, but the Welshman was to end the season on a high.

Victory at Rally Japan was his third of the campaign - the best return in any season to date for Evans who declared "it feels nice after last year".

With Rovanpera following Ogier's lead for 2024 in deciding not to contest a full calendar, surely this would be the year their Toyota team-mate would finally get to stand atop the WRC podium?

Sadly for Evans, the opening paragraph of the BBC report for the season's first race set the tone.

'Elfyn Evans faded to finish a disappointing third behind winner Thierry Neuville at Rallye Monte Carlo.'

As it turned out it was second place in the driver's championship come December, but it was another disappointing season for the Welsh driver, with Neuville instead becoming a first-time world champion after Evans' years of waiting.

And Evans, of course, was runner-up - though only just.

As Neuville lined up in Nagoya needing just six points - he collected 17 - to end his own streak of five championship runners-up spots, the Welshman began Rally Japan in third place.

For the second year in a row, Evans saved his best for last and a back-to-back Japanese victory brought a double silver lining.

Not only did it see him overhaul Ott Tanak to claim runners-up spot for a fourth time, it also saw Toyota snatch the manufacturer's championship.

However, the big personal prize remained as elusive as ever.

"We're sorry we couldn't deliver [the drivers'] championship," Evans said, "but we'll try again next year."

A revamp of the points system for 2025 was welcomed by Evans; it also brought his tightest title race yet.

After second place to Ogier in the Monte Carlo curtain-raiser, the re-energised Welshman won in Sweden and Kenya - rallies the Frenchman sat out.

With a 36-point advantage, Evans had opened up the largest championship lead ever recorded after three rounds of a WRC campaign.

But he would not win again that season and though he never finished lower than sixth, Ogier gradually whittled away at his lead until it came down to just three points with one round to go.

That race was a brand new entry to the calendar, and there was uncertainty over what lay ahead at Rally Saudi Arabia.

The terrain proved brutal for all the drivers. Tyre problems galore saw the leaderboard shifting like the sand. It ended with Ogier in third and Evans in sixth.

The points-swing was seven. The Frenchman had won a record-equalling ninth WRC title by four points, and Evans had fallen just short for the fifth time in six years.

"We've done what we can, that's it," was his reaction.

"We're competitors at the end of the day, we always want better, we always want more."

But there is only one more thing to do. Finally shake-off the tag of nearly-man.

He grabbed the 2026 championship lead with victory in February's Rally Sweden and has refused to let it go.

Once again his rivals are Toyota team-mates. This time it is Pajari, who won three rallies in a row, before Solberg triumphed in Rally Chile at the start of September to put himself back in the title reckoning.

Evans will require at most 19 points to guarantee him the title, but has not finished higher than third in the past five rallies since winning in Japan.

He will also have to cope with being first on the road in Sardinia - sweeping the gravel which has frequently caused him trouble in the past.

"I think especially with opening the road, normally in Sardinia it's a significant disadvantage to run first," concedes Evans who says he will "ignore the championship situation".

"You can't really afford to [think about the lead]. I have plenty of experience of what not to do," he muses.

"But you know how it turns out. I think it's far less certain than what it appears on paper."

True, but maybe by Sunday, the paper in the history books will show Evans finally proved he is not just another runner-up.

title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp after coach denies rift
description: Cristiano Ronaldo says he has left Portugal's international camp and will explain why "in time", hours after head coach Jorge Jesus denied any rift with the player.
fullText:
Cristiano Ronaldo says he has left Portugal's international camp and will explain the reasons why "in time".

It comes after head coach Jorge Jesus earlier said there was no rift with the captain, following claims the five-times Ballon d'Or winner had refused to train.

Ronaldo has said he considered retiring from international football after the World Cup in the summer but opted to continue as he chases down 1,000 career goals.

He was included in Jesus' 25-man squad for the current international break and started the opening Nations League game against Wales.

However, the Al-Nassr forward did not feature in Portugal's 2-1 win over Norway in Olso on Sunday and did not join his team-mates in going over to the visiting fans at the final whistle.

Instead, the former Real Madrid and Manchester United player headed to the changing rooms - prompting reports he was unhappy with the manager.

Speaking to media before Portugal's Nations League match against Denmark on Thursday, Jesus said: "There was no incident whatsoever.

"Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that."

Jesus said he had told Ronaldo before the match he would not be starting, but might be brought on later in the game.

"Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about," he added.

Former Benfica manager Jesus also dismissed suggestions Ronaldo had refused to train on Tuesday, saying the 41-year-old instead had to do individual exercises for "mobility" and "strengthening" but would train as normal on Wednesday.

However, Ronaldo did not join his team-mates on the pitch in Denmark with Portuguese media sharing a video of him leaving Parken stadium alongside two members of the backroom staff.

And the player later took to Instagram to announce his departure.

"After the press conference of the national team and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp," he wrote.

"In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave."

He added he wished his team-mates good luck in their forthcoming games.

Goncalo Ramos scored the winner against Norway and Jesus had said the AC Milan striker would again be preferred to Ronaldo against Denmark.

"If I need [Ronaldo], he'll come on. If I don't need him, he won't."

The Portuguese Football Federation later confirmed Ronaldo's departure in a statement which added: "Preparation for the two matches against Denmark and Norway continue as planned with the 24 remaining squad members.

"The entire delegation remains totally focussed on the national team's next fixtures and on achieving the established objectives."

What will new call-ups bring to Northern Ireland?
description: Before the upcoming 2027 Women's World Cup play-off with Portugal, what will the five new faces bring to Northern Ireland?
fullText:
When Northern Ireland run out to take on Portugal in their 2027 Women's World Cup play-off, they know they will be the underdogs.

That would be the case even if Michael McArdle had a full-strength squad to pick from, but he has had to deal with a lengthy injury list before the first play-off round.

However, disappointment for some leads to opportunities for others, and his 23-strong squad as produced five new names.

Sparta Pargue forward Kess Elmore was a surprise inclusion but her versatility could be key, while Galway United defender Lucy-Jayne Grant is another new face.

McArdle has also rewarded three Women's Premiership players - Naomi McLaughlin, Jane McMaster and Charlotte Havern - with their first call-ups.

But what can they all bring to the international stage?

Elmore and Grant named in Northern Ireland squad

With the absence of key attackers Simone Magill, who is back in training after having her first child, and Danielle Maxwell and Caragh Hamilton, who are injured, the introduction of Elmore to the squad is intriguing.

The 27-year-old Sparta Prague attacker qualifies for Northern Ireland through her father, who is from Lisburn.

Elmore came through Liverpool's academy and made the move to the USA in 2017 to play college football for the UConn Huskies and Oregon Ducks.

Her professional career started with Saint Etienne in France in 2023 and moved to Brooklyn FC for the inaugural USL Super League the following year.

Elmore has Champions League experience with Austrian champions St Polten against the likes of Chelsea and Lyon, and she moved to the Czech Republic in July.

Predominantly an attacking midfielder, Elmore can play right across the forward line and McArdle says "that versatility brings a strength to us".

"The biggest thing for Kess is the attacking prowess she's got as a creative player and an attacking player," said the Scot.

"She's coming in with good experience of playing against high quality opposition, and Portugal's squad is full of players that are at elite European clubs.

"Not speaking on behalf of Kess, but when you get that first call up at the age of 27 it is quite a special moment.

"It's been quite a special few weeks working with Kess in the background, so I'm looking forward to her joining camp and bringing those qualities to the group."

As well as Elmore, another player who has earned their first call-up is Cavan-born left back Lucy-Jayne Grant, who qualifies for Northern Ireland through her father.

The 22-year-old plays for Galway United in the League of Ireland, and she helped the club win the cross-border All-Island Cup in 2024.

McArdle said he had identified Grant for a possible call-up early into this time at the job, and she had earned her chance after he and his staff done their "due diligence".

"Over the summer she's performed well and she has spent time in the environment as a training player, so we have got to know her.

"She has broken through now on the left side of defence, so she'll add to the depth within there with the squad."

As well as her on-pitch ability, Galway's website says that Grant can juggle and is a qualified piano and violin teacher, so should be able to entertain the camp throughout the window.

Women's Premiership players featuring in senior Northern Ireland squads is nothing new.

In fact, before the historic Euro 2022 finals, it was the norm.

While more players have moved to England or Scotland over the past few years, the Irish League still plays a key role for the international team.

In McArdle's squad for the play-off, eight of his players are still based in Northern Ireland, and he has handed three of them first call-ups.

Attacking midfielder McLaughlin, 20, broke through at Sion Swifts before she moved to Cliftonville in 2024.

Her performances at Solitude earned her a move to Aberdeen in January but she returned to Northern Ireland with Glentoran in July, where she has impressed.

"Naomi has had a real purple patch since returning to Glentoran," McArdle said.

"It is exciting for her. She gives us another attacking option and a bit of versatility because she's slightly different to some of the players that are in the squad."

Full back McMaster, 22, has been a stalwart at Linfield and has been a key player in the club's push into title contention this season.

McMaster, who can also play in the centre of defence, has represented Northern Ireland before both at underage level and with the futsal team, but this is her opportunity to win a first senior cap.

"Jane has had a few consistent seasons and come through the international pathway," said McArdle.

"She is having a fantastic season with Linfield and deserves her call-up, which is exciting."

At 16, Havern is the youngest players in McArdle's squad and has earned a call-up after helping Cliftonville to a Premiership and League Cup double, and the Reds are also in the Irish Cup final.

Another underage international, it will be a chance for McArdle to work with the all-action midfielder first hand in the senior squad.

"Charlotte's impressive form with Cliftonville and has been a key part of their performances this season.

"They have helped Charlotte break through into the national team to get this experience."

title: Tom Curry extends Sale Sharks contract
description: England international flanker Tom Curry signs a two-year contract extension with Sale Sharks.
fullText:
England international flanker Tom Curry has signed a two-year contract extension with Sale Sharks.

The 28-year-old has spent his entire career with the Sharks and made his debut aged 18 in October 2016 and his new deal will keep him with the Prem side until the end of the 2027-28 campaign.

Director of rugby Alex Sanderson said Curry, whose identical twin brother Ben also plays for the club, is "fundamental" to the team.

"The terms are a couple of years and that's on Tom's desire to ensure that he's physically in the best spot to be able to honour his contract, to play a load of games for the next two years," Sanderson said.

"Then we both said we'll see where his body's at, at that point, with the want and desire for him to finish his career at Sale.

"He was the one, after some really honest conversations, that said we need to keep this group together, the core group together.

"He's fundamental to us, in terms of being the keystone, really, to that whole group."

Curry added: "Sale Sharks means everything to me and this is the club I have supported my whole life.

"I'm very proud of the hard work we've put in over the last 10 years to get the club to where it is now, but I know how much more we have to give and that's the reason I want to stay. There's no place I would rather be."

Curry, who has been capped 71 times by his country, missed the majority of the 2023-24 season after being diagnosed with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome - a condition that means the ball in the hip joint is not entirely round.

He underwent hip surgery in February 2024 and was warned his career could be over but returned to playing top level rugby just four months later.

In December of that year he had a stem-cell procedure with a view to him being able to play until the 2027 World Cup in Australia.

"He's surpassing expectations, his own medical expectations and what's gone before him in terms of the [hip] injury that he had," Sanderson added.

"We're not seeing any signs of wear and tear at this point and it might come in to factor later down the line but at this point he's as fresh and as mobile as he's ever been."

Meanwhile, Sharks summer signing Courtney Lawes, who made his Prem debut for the side in the 34-24 home defeat by Bristol at the weekend, said earlier this month that players who choose to go abroad should remain eligible for England selection.

Lawes, has won 105 England caps and returned to England this summer, having spent two years at French side Brive where he was ineligible to represent his country.

At present, the Rugby Football Union does not permit players not playing in this country to be picked for Steve Borthwick's national side, other than in exceptional circumstances.

Toulouse back row Jack Willis, who has retained his award as the best player in France's Top 14, has not played for England since 2023 but said this week "it's something I still want to do".

However, Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter has said he does not think the rules should be changed and Sanderson said altering the approach could lead to the Prem being "devastated".

"I just think it would devalue our the Prem, which we know is a really good product with really competitive teams, too much if players were allowed to take the pay cheque, move to France and then get the Eurostar over for training with the international team," he said.

"I think it would devastate the Prem because then players can literally have the cake and eat it, can't they? They can take the pay cheque and there'll be no consequence for playing outside of the country.

"I understand the views of those lads who feel otherwise and we have some in our quarters.

"I'm looking at from a different point of view, from a director of rugby that wants the players and we wouldn't be able to compete to keep them on the books if we had to go against some of the juggernauts of the Top 14."

title: Ex-world champion boxer Liam Smith charged with GBH
description: The 38-year-old was arrested after an alleged attack on an apartment building's night concierge.
fullText:
Former world champion boxer Liam Smith has been charged with causing grievous bodily harm after an alleged attack on a night concierge at a luxury Manchester apartment building.

Smith, who held the WBO light-middleweight title from 2015 to 2016, was arrested after the man suffered serious facial injuries at The Blade on Silvercroft Street in Deansgate on 13 September, police confirmed.

The 38-year-old appeared at Manchester Magistrates Court the following day charged with causing GBH with intent, and was released on bail.

Smith, from Liverpool, is next due to appear at Manchester Crown Court on 19 October, where he will be asked to enter a plea.

The alleged victim reportedly suffered fractures and required surgery.

Smith, nicknamed Beefy, had been due to make a comeback fight against local fighter Ilaru Kujala in Finland on 4 September.

However, he withdrew from the fight a few days earlier after suffering a calf injury, according to reports.

Smith has fought at the highest levels, including against elite champions such as Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez.

More recently he fought British rival Chris Eubank Jr in two memorable bouts, defeating the Brighton man in the first fight in January 2023 before suffering a defeat in the rematch eight months later.

title: Oil shipments are recovering, but damaged refineries keep fuel prices high
description:
Crude oil is moving through the Strait of Hormuz at a pace that is starting to approach prewar levels, a notable rebound for the world’s most critical oil choke point. 
That restored flow is mainly the result of Iran’s somewhat depleted military capability and a U.S. Navy operation that has secured a portion of the waterway for relatively secure passage.

fullText:
Crude oil is moving through the Strait of Hormuz at a pace that is starting to approach prewar levels, a notable rebound for the world's most critical oil choke point.

That restored flow is mainly the result of Iran's somewhat depleted military capability and a U.S. Navy operation that has secured a portion of the waterway for relatively secure passage.

But the forces driving high fuel prices are not receding along with the development. That will require a lot more than the costly military campaign that is clearing the way for passage of one product at one particular moment in the war.

Most of the refined gasoline and diesel that was moving through the strait before the war is still not getting shipped, a major factor keeping prices elevated.

The rebound of crude shipments "is good news, but we are far from out of the woods," said Bob McNally, founder of the research firm Rapidan Energy Group. "The market realizes that. We have dug ourselves into a deep deficit over the last several months, and this only reduces it. It does not get us back to where we were."

Crude oil prices dipped Tuesday - largely as a response to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resuming limited operations. The price of Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil, remained above $100 a barrel Wednesday morning, roughly 40 percent higher than it was when the Iran war began in February.

The outlook for the war and for oil was further clouded on Wednesday, when the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported that three vessels carrying fuel through a corridor of the strait the U.S. military has been trying to protect had been attacked the day before.

Meanwhile, the price of a gallon of regular gas in the United States is averaging $4.43, and diesel is at $6.41, according to AAA.

Analysts warn that even sustained deliveries of crude through the Strait of Hormuz at prewar levels would not do much to meaningfully bring down global prices in the coming weeks.

They note that oil inventories are depleted and need to be replenished. Refining infrastructure in the Middle East has been badly damaged and will take time to repair - all the while remaining vulnerable to further attacks.

As a result of that constrained capacity, gasoline and diesel shipments through the strait - crucial to bringing prices down for consumers - remain just a fraction of what they were before the war.

"Nobody consumes crude oil directly," said Mark Finley, an oil markets scholar at Rice University's Baker Institute for Public Policy. "It has to be made into something useful, like diesel or jet fuel or gasoline. The world's refining system that turns crude oil into useful products is severely strained."

As if to punctuate the point that the emergency is not over and inventories of everything are running low, the U.S. Energy Department on Tuesday announced it would release another 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which is already at its lowest level since 1983.

"We have dug ourselves into a big hole," Finley said.

There is general agreement in the oil industry that most of the crude still getting blocked in the Strait of Hormuz is Iranian, and that is by design. The U.S. is trying to put economic pressure on the regime and choke off its funding stream for its military activities.

As far as how much non-Iranian crude is getting through, ship tracking firms offer somewhat different estimates.

According to Kpler, the week ending Sept. 27 averaged nearly 12.5 million barrels per day, just 1 million barrels below the "pre-war baseline."

Windward, another ship tracking platform, estimated closer to 10 million barrels per day.

"This is not trivial," said Ami Daniel, Windward's co-founder and CEO. "The U.S. military has done a fantastic job facilitating consistent shipments."

The amount of oil getting through, though, does continue to swing wildly. There were days in September where only a few million barrels transited the strait, according to ship tracking data.

The restored flows depend on extremely costly U.S. Navy assistance and dark-fleet work-arounds that could unravel with a renewed Iranian military campaign.

Markets remain skeptical that the shipments of crude can continue at prewar levels absent a major diplomatic breakthrough between the U.S. and Iran.

"Maintaining the American military presence required to keep significant volumes of oil moving through the Strait comes at an enormous financial and operational cost," Danny Citrinowicz, a Middle East security scholar at the Atlantic Council, posted Tuesday on X.

"The real test is whether Washington can turn its military advantage into a durable situation in which oil flows normally, insurance and transportation costs decline, the extraordinary U.S. military deployment can be reduced, and Iran effectively loses Hormuz as a tool of strategic coercion," Citrinowicz wrote. "We are not there yet."

Even full restoration of shipping through the strait, McNally warned, would not bring markets back to where they were at the beginning of the year.

Iran has shifted its attacks away from the strait toward oil infrastructure on land, which in some cases can be even more damaging. One such recent attack disabled Saudi Arabia's key East-West pipeline, which had been delivering 7 million barrels of crude each day. The pipeline has been only partially restored, and analysts say it remains extremely vulnerable to further targeting.

"Iran may be losing control of Hormuz, but it retains the ability to disable critical infrastructure," McNally said. "This progress can be quickly offset by the Iranians and their allies hitting those fixed assets."

Karen DeYoung contributed to this report.

title: France midfielder Koné 'shocked' by coach Zidane's ability in training
description: France midfielder Manu Koné had to pinch himself when new coach Zinedine Zidane laced up his boots to take part in training.  Arguably the world’s best playmaker during his heyday, the 54-year-old Zidane was in his element spraying passes around and whipping in crosses to his awe-struck players.  “Seeing it in person is even better, especially at his age,” the 25-year-old Koné added.
fullText:
PARIS (AP) — France midfielder Manu Koné had to pinch himself when new coach Zinedine Zidane laced up his boots to take part in training.

Arguably the world's best playmaker during his heyday, the 54-year-old Zidane was in his element spraying passes around and whipping in crosses to his awe-struck players.

"What shocked me during the first week of training was his technical range. He's lost none of his ability," Koné said on Tuesday ahead of Friday's game against Italy at Stade de France in the Nations League.

"Seeing it in person is even better, especially at his age," the 25-year-old Koné added. "It's true that I was little when he was near the end of his career. To see that he still has that technique now means it must have been incredible in his era."

Zidane's two goals in the 1998 World Cup final win against Brazil made him an overnight superstar, with his face famously beamed on the Arc de Triomphe in Paris as a nation celebrated. A Ballon d'Or award followed and, two years later, his superb performances led Les Bleus to more glory at the European Championship.

"It's a pleasure to be coached by Zidane, a world legend. He's told me to play freely and given me confidence," Koné added. "He was a midfielder, so as a midfielder I listen to everything he says and I can only learn by his side. He advises me a lot about my positioning and gives me more responsibility."

Zidane's last performance for France was in the 2006 World Cup final, which ended in a penalty shootout loss to Italy. Even though Zidane was sent off in extra time for head-butting Italy defender Marco Materazzi when France was dominating, it did not affect his popularity among French soccer fans.

Since his arrival Zidane has been in the spotlight even more than some of the stars in his squad.

"We shouldn't be shocked, you can only congratulate him for his career," Koné said. "We will see that on Friday, the ovation he gets (against Italy)."

Zidane played Koné in a sentry midfield role in a 1-0 win at Turkey last Friday, which meant largely sitting in front of and protecting the defense with limited scope to push up.

Two weeks ago, Koné scored twice for Roma against Inter Milan in a table-topping Serie A clash but has yet to find the net in 21 appearances for Les Bleus.

"The goal will come," he said. "But the important thing is to meet the coach's requirements." ___

title: Bayern Munich set to offer Michael Olise new long-term contract to deter interest from other clubs
description: Bayern Munich are set to offer French international attacking midfielder Michael Olise (24) a new long-term contract to extend his stay with the club, according to a report from BILD. The Bundesliga g...
fullText:
Bayern Munich are set to offer French international attacking midfielder Michael Olise (24) a new long-term contract to extend his stay with the club, according to a report from BILD. The Bundesliga giants are aiming to retain the services of the former Crystal Palace playmaker and deter interest from other clubs after a summer transfer window fuelled with rumours regarding his long-term future in Bavaria.

Real Madrid were at the front of the queue to sign the 24-year-old during the summer transfer window. However, with Bayern refusing to negotiate with the La Liga outfit, the Spanish capital club were forced to look elsewhere to reinforce the options of Jose Mourinho. PSG were also linked with a move for the Frenchman. Even now the window has closed, the rumour mill continues to link the attacking midfielder with a move away from Germany.

In a bid to extend the attacker's stay in the Bundesliga, Bayern Munich are preparing to offer Olise a contract extension with a substantial pay rise. If the Chelsea academy graduate was to accept the terms, this would extend his stay in Bavaria for a further 6 years. His current contract is set to expire in 2029.

title: From future number one to top of Dortmund’s wishlist: Nine Germany players who could debut against Serbia
description: Jürgen Klopp’s Germany era started with underwhelming results and performances against the Netherlands and Greece, but the extended international break is mainly used to experiment, with five playe...
fullText:
Jürgen Klopp's Germany era started with underwhelming results and performances against the Netherlands and Greece, but the extended international break is mainly used to experiment, with five players already making their senior international debuts.

That number will certainly increase when the four-time World Cup winners face Serbia and Greece in the first week of October. Here is the list of players who could follow in the footsteps of Philipp Treu, Younes Ebnoutalib, Yannik Engelhardt, Bambasé Conté and Hennes Behrens.

Jonas Urbig (23, GK, FC Bayern)

Including his selection to accompany the 59-year-old in the pre-match press conference, all signs are pointing towards Urbig making his debut in Germany's goal against Serbia. FC Bayern's shot-stopper is touted to be Manuel Neuer's long-term replacement at both club and country level.

With the 41-year-old facing multiple setbacks, Urbig has already featured 34 times for the Rekordmeister, including 20 Bundesliga starts. Klopp confirmed that he'll be behind Marc-André ter Stegen in the pecking order, but the former Köln goalie will be expected to make his international debut on Thursday at Allianz Arena.

Köln prodigy El Mala was in the headlines throughout the entire summer transfer market. Both Brentford and Borussia Dortmund were very close to agreeing to a deal with Köln, but the 20-year-old attacker eventually extended his contract.

However, like Köln's legendary number ten Lukas Podolski, he'll surely leave the club in the near future if he maintains his current performance level. Julian Nagelsmann did nominate El Mala for the national team during the World Cup qualifiers, but he was only an unused substitute in the win over Luxembourg.

Finn Jeltsch (20, CB, Stuttgart)

Another uncapped 20-year-old in Klopp's second squad, Jeltsch is on FC Bayern's wishlist for quite some time. The 2024/25 DFB-Pokal winner started all six games for Stuttgart at the start of the season.

The Nürnberg academy product could return to Bavaria if the move to the German giants finally materialized, although recent reports added Real Madrid and Arsenal to the race. Including captaining the U21 side, Jeltsch played a total of 43 games for Germany youth national teams.

The central midfielder is one of the surprise inclusions in Klopp's extended squad for his first four games in charge of Germany. From the previous six Germans in Celtic's history, only the right-back Andreas Hinkel played for the national team while he was still at the club.

Baur joined the Scottish champions after helping Paderborn to a Bundesliga promotion. While Celtic's start to the campaign left plenty to ponder with yet another Champions League elimination and defeats to fierce rivals Rangers, he personally settled well at his first club outside Germany.

Vitaly Janelt (28, CM, Brentford)

If he gets his chance either against Serbia or Greece, Janelt will be Klopp's oldest debutant among the outfield players. The 28-year-old conceded that he was very close to giving up on waiting for his first international call.

In addition to the extended squad list, Brentford's unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign certainly helped the Hamburg-born midfielder in ending that wait. Janelt played every minute so far this season as he scored in the first two home games before captaining his side against Bournemouth and Chelsea before the international break.

Felix Keidel (23, DM, Elversberg)

The all-rounder was playing 3. Liga football with Ingolstadt in the 2024/25 season. When he left his childhood club in a move that cost Elversberg €400k, there was no way he'd expect such a quick turnaround in his career.

After helping the minnows to their first-ever promotion to the Bundesliga, Keidel scored against Borussia Mönchengladbach with a spectacular free-kick. The 23-year-old has never played for Germany youth national teams before receiving Klopp's surprising call.

Derry Scherhant (23, LW, Freiburg)

After Treu's excellent debut, Scherhant could be the next Freiburg star to make his first appearance for Germany. The former Hertha BSC winger displaced Freiburg's legend Vincenzo Grifo from the starting lineup with his strong start to the campaign.

The 23-year-old attacker already registered nine direct goal contributions across three competitions for Julian Schuster's overachieving side. Florian Wirtz was Nagelsmann's preferred option on the left wing during the World Cup, while Scherhant will now compete with El Mala, Kevin Schade and Chris Führich for regular squad spots.

Finn Dahmen (28, GK, Augsburg) and Noah Atubolu (24, GK, Freiburg)

Although it's highly unlikely that they will play against Serbia, either Dahmen or Atubolu could get a chance away in Greece. Both Marc ter Stegen and Alexander Nübel left the squad after playing a game each in the first two fixtures of the UEFA Nations League campaign.

Dahmen and Atubolu are now ahead of Oliver Baumann, who was Germany's number one before Neuer's return from retirement for the World Cup, but they will most likely miss out when Klopp announces his 23-man squad for the next international break in November.

title: Elmore and Grant named in Northern Ireland squad

fullText:
Sparta Prague forward Kess Elmore is a surprise first call-up for Northern Ireland's 2027 Women's World Cup play-off with Portugal.

Elmore, 27, is a former England youth international and is one of five new call-ups in Michael McArdle's squad.

Galway United full back Lucy-Jayne Grant is included for the first time, as are the Irish Premiership trio Naomi McLaughlin, Jane McMaster and Charlotte Havern.

Havern has had a strong campaign for champions Cliftonville, while McMaster has stood out for Linfield and McLaughlin has impressed for Glentoran after a mid-season switch back to the league from Aberdeen.

There are several absentees through injury, including Kelsie Burrows, Laura Rafferty, Nadene Caldwell, Megan Bell, Joely Andrews, Danielle Maxwell and Caragh Hamilton.

Northern Ireland host Portugal at Inver Park on Friday, 9 October before the return leg in Portimao four days later.

The sides last met in Euro 2025 qualifying when Portugal ran out 4-0 winners in Liera before a narrow 2-1 victory at Mourneview Park.

If McArdle's side can upset Portugal, who are ranked 28 places higher than NI, then they would face Iceland or Croatia in the next play-off round.

While the majority of teams who win the second play-off round will progress to the finals in Brazil, Northern Ireland's ranking means they would likely face an additional inter-continental play-off round in February, as the lowest European side, if they are to make a first World Cup.

title: How do teams deal with longer international window?
description: With the international window extended to four games, how do nations like Northern Ireland deal with the additional demands on players and staff?
fullText:
In years gone by, the final whistle would have blown in Northern Ireland's Nations League game with Hungary and the players would have been heading back to their clubs.

Instead, Michael O'Neill and his squad are back on the road to Slovakia to face Ukraine in the extended international window.

For 2026, the September and October breaks have been amalgamated into one 16-day window, with four fixtures instead of two.

Northern Ireland have made a strong start to the campaign with four points from two matches, but it isn't without its challenges.

But how does it impact a nation like Northern Ireland, who do not have the squad depth or resources of some of Europe's heavy hitters?

Szoboszlai's Hungary latest to draw blank in Belfast

O'Neill 'positive' as NI maintain unbeaten start

For Northern Ireland in particular, the schedule has been gruelling.

Their Nations League campaign started with a 5,000-mile round trip to Georgia, where Shea Charles' 99th-minute winner snatched a late victory.

For that game, O'Neill, his staff and players had stayed in the BST time zone instead of trying to adapt to the three-hour time difference.

With a short turnaround before Monday's game against Hungary - their first home match in 315 days - the squad flew back home overnight to arrive back in Belfast on Saturday morning.

While Northern Ireland kept Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai quiet - as they did with Paris St-Germain star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in Tbilisi - the players looked tired as the game progressed.

"Tiredness will be a big factor," O'Neill said.

"Logistics are a big factor as well in terms of your travel and how that works."

One other factor for smaller nations is injuries and suspensions.

Northern Ireland were already without key players such as Conor Bradley and Ali McCann before Sunderland defender Daniel Ballard injured his hamstring in Georgia, ruling him out of the rest of the window.

Unlike Germany boss Jurgen Klopp, who has the luxury of effectively selecting two different squads, O'Neill has to work with a smaller playing pool.

Of course, injuries are part of the game and can happen at any moment, but the condensed window only magnifies the issue.

"It's a massive factor in the game and if you look at some players who have been injured in the first game, like Dan, they are now out completely," O'Neill said.

"Other countries have had that as well, but you can miss four games of a six-game tournament."

Another factor to consider is an increase in yellow cards, with tired legs leading to a higher chance of picking up a second booking, which would lead to a suspension.

After two matches, seven Northern Ireland players are one card away from missing a match, and O'Neill admitted he found some of the yellows handed out to his side as "disappointing".

While this is the first iteration of the autumnal quadruple header, O'Neill says he would like to see consistency across the scheduling of matches.

Georgia, for example, have had their first two matches at home so have had limited travel and, by consequence, easier recovery from matches before they head to Hungary and Belfast for their final two games of the window.

"There are things in there that create a bit of an imbalance and I know it's difficult to get the fixtures all right," O'Neill said.

"The only thing I would like to see is we have an extra day's recovery now going into the third game.

"I would like to see the recovery periods between every game be consistent."

The consolation for Northern Ireland is that Ukraine will be making that same journey back from Tbilisi before the third game, but the caveat is they have an additional day to recover and have an hour less to travel with the time difference.

O'Neill added that he understands the logic behind the scheduling, but it has "high demands on players in that time".

"It might be difficult to do that [have consistent gaps between games] but I think that would help a lot of the teams, particularly the smaller nations," he said.

"Sixteen days is a long time and there's the travel as well, obviously.

"We're coping well with it, but I think it will be a tough game for us on Friday night."

While Europe's bigger nations have their own in-house resources, countries like Northern Ireland share staff with clubs, which can bring its own challenges in an extended window.

"We don't carry full-time doctors, full-time physios and full-time sports scientists," O'Neill added.

"Other countries are the same, but all our staff work at clubs and we need agreement from the clubs.

"That's a challenge to be able to staff it properly and keep the level of professionalism.

"The big countries don't have that, they have full-time staff and an army of staff to be able to do these things."

O'Neill also has to consider how much to rotate this squad. It's a fine balance between keeping key players fresh, but also how much exposure to give his young squad.

Of the 26-man squad, 17 of the players are aged 25 or under and only three - Josh Magennis (36), Paddy McNair (31) and Dion Charles (30) - are over the age of 30.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill, Everton's Braiden Graham and Kieran Morrison, who is on loan at Sheffield Wednesday from Liverpool, are the three teenagers in the squad.

"I don't want to put too many young players on the pitch in a game like that where they're untried and untested at that level," O'Neill said.

"We want to bring the younger players in to give them the best chance to be able to do well and to build their confidence and to build their reputation. That's the challenge for us."

title: Fishlock set for Wales return - but not as player
description: Rhian Wilkinson says icon Jess Fishlock will be back with the national team if they reach a World Cup play-off final in December – but only as a coach.
fullText:
Rhian Wilkinson says in-form Wales icon Jess Fishlock will be back with the national team if they reach a Women's World Cup play-off final in December – but only as a coach.

Fishlock, Wales' most-capped footballer, called time on her international career last October.

But the 39-year-old continues to shine for Seattle Reign, having claimed two fine goals in last weekend's win over Boston Legacy to become the National Women's Soccer League club's all-time leading scorer.

Wales, meanwhile, are without a string of senior players for the World Cup play-off semi-final against Albania next month, but Wilkinson says she has turned down Fishlock's tongue-in-cheek offer to come out of international retirement.

"Jess could play forever, she's incredible," the Wales head coach said.

"There was never a doubt that Jess Fishlock could still do a job for us. [But] I think it was absolutely the right time for her to step away after that amazing qualification for the Euro [last year]."

Women's World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales Extra, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Fishlock, who has said this will be her last year playing club football, will be on duty with Reign when Wales go to Albania on Friday, 9 October and then again in the return leg in Llanelli four days later.

Should Wales overcome a side who are 36 places in the Fifa rankings – and one they beat twice in the group phase of World Cup qualifying – they will play either Norway or Romania in a two-legged play-off final in December.

Wilkinson has revealed that another recently retired former player, Kayleigh Barton, will be part of her staff for the Albania ties and then Fishlock will have a role should Wales reach the final.

Fishlock previously worked as a technical assistant for Wales' opening game of this qualifying campaign, against the Czech Republic in March.

Wilkinson explained that Fishlock had been in touch before she named her semi-final squad on Tuesday, adding: "I didn't appreciate her saying 'call me up coach, I'm ready', which I thought was mean, but [she was] a wonderful player and a great leader for us.

"If we are able to get past Albania, she'll be coming in as a coach for us for the next round."

title: Young U.S. men's soccer team has ups and downs in 4-2 victory over Chile
description: But all in all, it was another good result and fun outing for a program returning from the World Cup with the second of four friendlies over 11 days.
fullText:
ST. LOUIS — Amid all the excitement about his young U.S. soccer team, a wide-eyed crew that started the new World Cup cycle with an enlightening performance over the weekend, Mauricio Pochettino warned there would be ups and downs along the way.

After all, almost half the roster had never played at the senior level and, as a whole, the group hadn't spent much time together.

Tuesday's 4-2 victory over Chile at bubbly Energizer Park reinforced the coach's admonition.

The gorgeous build-up on the first goal.

Sebastian Berhalter and Gio Reyna putting their stamp on another match.

Teenager Julian Hall's second goal in two appearances, and teenager Mathis Albert scoring his first.

Chris Richards' 72nd-minute tiebreaking goal as part of a second-half comeback.

All in all, it was another good result and fun outing for a program returning from the World Cup with the second of four friendlies over 11 days. For the second time in four days, the Americans scored four goals and flexed their muscles against a South American foe.

There were troubling moments, as well, particularly in the first half, when the Americans conceded numerous scoring opportunities and made many mistakes. They were fortunate to be tied at intermission.

But they showed resilience in the second half and, coupled with the 4-1 thumping of Peru last Saturday in Orlando, continued building momentum heading into this Saturday's showdown with rival Mexico in greater Phoenix. They will also play Canada on Oct. 6 in St. Paul, Minnesota.

In a pregame ceremony in his hometown, World Cup captain Tim Ream was honored for 16 years and 86 appearances with the national team. The Charlotte FC center back, who will turn 39 on Friday, announced moments earlier that he has retired from international soccer and won't weigh his club future until after the MLS season.

"The kids are getting younger and younger," he said. Ream was talking about the U.S. roster, not his own three kids.

"I actually got a text message last night [that] I was a senior at Saint Louis University when [17-year-old forward Cavan Sullivan] was born," Ream said. "I was like, 'He's only four years older than my oldest.'"

Ream was not selected to the current roster.

The starting lineup Tuesday averaged just over 23 years old, including teenagers Hall, Neil Pierre and Adri Mehmeti. The other young starters were midfielder Brooklyn Raines, 21, and right back Frankie Westfield, 20.

At almost 6-foot-7, the 18-year-old Pierre was unmistakable on the backline. Like Sullivan, he is enjoying a breakout club campaign with the Philadelphia Union.

Reyna was the only holdover starter from the Peru match. Like Saturday, Pochettino started six 2026 World Cup players: Reyna, Berhalter, goalkeeper Chris Brady, wingers Antonee Robinson and Sergiño Dest, and center back Miles Robinson.

Brady, 22, made his first international start after debuting as a sub in a World Cup tuneup.

Chile — which has missed three World Cups since winning the 2016 Copa America — was without captain Gabriel Suazo and Lucas Cepeda, La Liga-based players red-carded in the 1-0 loss to Canada on Saturday in Toronto.

As they did against Peru, the Americans threatened early off a Reyna set piece. His free kick from 25 yards met Miles Robinson for a point-blank header that Lawrence Vigouroux slapped aside in spectacular fashion.

The U.S. was organized and energetic at the start but not always precise. In the 18th minute, a miscommunication between Berhalter and Mehmeti led to a Chilean threat. A minute later, Berhalter's tasty through ball sent Hall in alone, but after rounding Vigouroux, his off-balanced, angled bid missed high and wide.

Brady was shaky, sitting back when he should've come forward and allowing Victor Méndez to test him. Then, on shots a minute apart, he also got lucky as Ben Brereton's screamer dinged the crossbar and Darío Osorio's low bid hit the far post.

Against the run of play, the match took an unforeseen turn.

Two minutes after Osorio's scare, the Americans went ahead in the 37th on a wonderfully constructed goal. They won the ball in midfield. Dest and Reyna played a sharp combination. With quick and clever footwork, Dest danced into the box. He crossed to Hall, who dummied the ball with the smarts of a veteran, allowing Berhalter to bury a 12-yarder into the far post.

Brady's problems continued. On the last act of the half — a Chilean corner kick — he punched the ball up, then backward. A mad scramble ensued. Finally, from inside the six-yard box, Diego Ulloa's side-volley caromed off Westfield's arm and into the net.

Brady's night — or nightmare — was over. As he did against Peru, Pochettino changed his goalkeeper at halftime: FC Cincinnati's Brian Schwake made his first appearance, becoming the 12th debut in this camp.

He couldn't do much about Maxi Gutiérrez's go-ahead goal in the 49th minute. Westfield's misstruck header in midfield allowed Gutiérrez to glide into the U.S. end. Berhalter failed to shut him down, and the Chilean forward whistled a 23-yard shot into the far corner with pinpoint accuracy.

Two minutes later, the U.S. answered. Reyna lifted a gentle cross into the box, where Hall rose from eight yards and headed it into the far side.

Pochettino turned to his bench and made seven subs, including five veterans. Vigouroux made a fine foot save on Antonee Robinson, but on the ensuing corner kick, Berhalter delivered a perfect ball to Richards for a powerful header from the edge of the six-yard box.

Chile threatened to pull even. The U.S. extended the lead on Albert's stab off the underside of the crossbar from close range. The announced crowd of 21,680 loved it.

Just before the final whistle, a benches-emptying scuffle broke out after a Chilean player tapped the fallen Schwake on the arm with his foot. Play resumed, but at the final whistle, another brief incident broke out.

"Take Me Home, Country Roads" boomed over the speakers.

Winger Cole Campbell, a first-time camper held out of the Peru match for an undisclosed ailment, and goalkeeper Diego Kochen, who played the second half Saturday, were not in uniform. Kochen was healthy, but Pochettino chose to dress 26 players again.

In his 60th appearance, Antonee Robinson captained the team for the first time.

Sullivan replaced Berhalter in the 83rd minute.

The Americans are 11-1-3 in greater St. Louis, including 5-0-0 at Energizer Park, which sits 1.3 miles directly west of the Gateway Arch and opened before the 2023 MLS season.

title: 'Paying attention in age of clickbait' – 2027 World Communications Day theme
description: The Vatican Dicastery for Communication releases the theme for the 2027 World Communications Day, which is “A New Gaze: Paying Attention in the Age of ...
fullText:
On the feast of St. Gabriel the Archangel, the Holy See’s Dicastery for Communication released the theme for the 61st World Communications Day.

The theme will be “A New Gaze: Paying Attention in the Age of Clickbait,” according to a press release published on Tuesday by the Dicastery (our parent organization).

This year’s theme invites Christians to open ourselves to “a conversion of our gaze: to look again, with attention and with love.”

“The attention economy, with its struggle for a few moments of interest amid the rapid and endless flow of content, is transforming not only our cognitive abilities but also the depth of our interpersonal communication,” it noted.

Only by paying attention to others with love can we see the “world, others, even ourselves, as Christ sees us: called by name and loved.”

“Our communication changes when our gaze chooses to encounter others rather than judge them,” said the statement.

People are inundated every moment of every day with expectations of rapid reactions and superficial relationships, resulting in a lack of genuine attention fueled by digital culture, it added.

“Yet attention is a precious form of generosity: the word ‘attention’ comes from ad-tendere—to reach out toward the other and toward the truth,” said the press release. “Christian communication can rediscover attention as both a gift and a way of seeing—the gaze of Jesus, who saw and allowed Himself to be touched.”

Rather than seeking to capture attention, communicating is about safeguarding attention “as a precious resource for relationships.”

In our modern age of “clickbait,” Christians are invited to pay attention and rediscover a healthy form of attention to one another.

“Communication is not just about words,” concluded the press release. “It involves the entire person and asks us to look, hear, and feel again in order to answer Christ’s call.”

World Communications Day 2027 takes place in many parts of the world—including the United States, England and Wales, France, Spain, Poland, and Italy—on May 9, but is celebrated on different days in various parts of the world, as set by the national Bishops’ Conferences.

title: Former world snooker champion Dott jailed for child sexual abuse
description: The 49-year-old was found guilty of two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010.
fullText:
Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been jailed for seven years after being convicted of child sexual abuse.

Judge Lord Harrower said Dott robbed his victims of "a significant part of their childhood" and said his behaviour bore the hallmarks of grooming.

Dott had denied two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010 but was found guilty following a trial at the High Court in Glasgow.

The 49-year-old Scot, who won the world snooker title in 2006, showed no emotion as he was sentenced, only nodding to someone in the public gallery as he was led away.

Lord Harrower told the High Court in Edinburgh that each of Dott's victims were vulnerable for reasons beyond their age.

He said Dott rewarded the victims with treats and disguised his abuse as being part of a game.

The former snooker champion was 16 or 17 when he abused the girl, who was about nine when her ordeal began.

Dott's abuse of the second victim - a boy aged about eight - began about 10 years later.

The court heard that he warned them they would not be believed if they told anyone about his actions.

As it happened: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott sentenced

The judge added Dott's victims had experienced "overwhelming emotions of fear, shame and anger" as a result of the abuse, affecting their mental health into adulthood.

Dott's behaviour towards the children "involved a gross violation of trust".

As Lord Harrower addressed him, Dott repeatedly shook his head in apparent disbelief.

The judge added social work reports have deemed Dott poses a "below average risk of reoffending", but as he still maintains his innocence, Lord Harrower could not take into account any remorse from Dott.

The court also heard that Dott has already been the subject of threats and has been moved within prison as a result.

Euan Dow, representing Dott, told the court the father-of-two was now separated from his wife but "continues to enjoy the support of his family and friends".

He added Dott suffers from "long-standing mental health issues" and that his personal and professional reputations had been destroyed.

The sentence of seven years has been backdated to 24 August, which is when the 49-year-old was remanded in custody.

He will spend the rest of his life on the sex offenders register.

Procurator Fiscal Faye Cook, of the Crown Office, said: "Graeme Dott achieved success and public admiration but, in private, he exploited the trust of two children to abuse and coerce them.

"Dott's criminal behaviour has been his downfall and he now faces the consequences of his actions."

She added that "justice has no time limit" and encouraged any victims of historical abuse to report it.

During the trial, the court heard that Dott had exposed himself and inappropriately touched a primary school girl in the 1990s and attacked a young boy between 2006 and 2010.

Dott called the allegations made against him "disgusting".

The girl, now a woman in her 40s, said Dott had "caressed" her bottom while giving her a piggyback and that, on another occasion, he had exposed himself to her.

On another occasion, she said Dott, of Glasgow, suggested she "take her trousers down" and lifted her top and began kissing her stomach after asking if she wanted to "play a guessing game".

The victim said Dott would kiss her, touch her inappropriately and carried out a sexual act that would, if committed now, amount to rape.

She said she recalled the "smell" of creams Dott used for a skin condition after he kissed her and that the actions left her "shocked and scared".

The court heard that Dott bought her a teddy bear with a love heart on it in the course of the abuse.

Police previously contacted Dott about the allegations in 2001, but no charges were brought.

The woman gave a new statement to police in 2025.

During his evidence, Dott's male victim said the abuse began shortly after Dott defeated Peter Ebdon to win his sole world title at The Crucible in Sheffield in 2006.

The boy, now a man in his 20s, said he was about eight years old when Dott molested him in a shower at a home in South Lanarkshire.

He told the court that Dott "rewarded" him with crisps and fizzy drinks and once handed him a £50 note, only to accuse the boy of stealing it when his parents found out he had the money.

He also said he was abused in a car on a number of occasions and "inappropriately touched" while Dott played online poker.

Dott was convicted of lewd and libidinous practices, which refer to any sexual crimes against children committed prior to 1 December 2010.

The offence was abolished in 2009, but is still used for crimes carried out before then.

Following his conviction in August, the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association said it had permanently revoked Dott's membership with immediate effect.

Dott was previously suspended from all professional snooker activities on 9 April 2025 pending the outcome of his trial.

He was subsequently relegated from the professional ranking list at the conclusion of the 2025/26 season.

Dott has two previous convictions for minor road traffic offences in 2013 and 2015.

title: Time for Tuchel to offer Alexander-Arnold some trust
description: Having been overlooked for so long, Trent Alexander-Arnold produced a world-class moment on his return, writes Phil McNulty.
fullText:
England head coach Thomas Tuchel's apparent lack of trust in Trent Alexander-Arnold has been one of the defining features - and a constant narrative - of his time in charge.

The 27-year-old right-back has won a Premier League title at Liverpool then moved to Real Madrid since he last started for England, selected as a left-back by interim manager Lee Carsley when scoring in a 3-1 Nations League win in Finland in October 2024.

He was ignored for England's World Cup squad last summer, despite right-back being a cursed role for Tuchel, making it appear that whatever questions the German had about that position, Alexander-Arnold was never going to be the answer.

So Tuchel's decision to recall Alexander-Arnold for this four-game Nations League camp came as a surprise, so emphatically had he been marginalised by England.

It was against this backdrop that Alexander-Arnold became the ninth right-back used by Tuchel in 24 games when he finally got his start against Czech Republic in Prague as England tried to recover from the 3-2 loss to World Cup holders Spain at Wembley.

And, with perhaps something to prove according to Tuchel, Alexander-Arnold did exactly that in one world-class moment that might convince his coach to train his sights on what he can do rather than what he cannot.

It is time, in other words, for Tuchel to offer Alexander-Arnold some trust.

Who continues to show how important they are? England player ratings

Kane and Gordon give England win over Czech Republic in Nations League

England, despite being in control, were toiling against the 10-man Czechs, who had seen danger man Pavel Sulc sent off after only 25 minutes for a reckless challenge on Elliot Anderson.

It was then, two minutes after the break, that Alexander-Arnold delivered a moment beyond those Tuchel has chosen ahead of him at right-back to pierce that stubborn resistance.

The player now officially known as "Trent", according to the name on the back of his shirt, had already made a 70-yard run into an attacking position in an attempt to increase England's attacking options.

When the move broke down, he regained possession before unfurling a magnificent right-foot delivery that floated in a teasing arc beyond three Czech defenders for Anthony Gordon to score with a stooping header that he made look far easier than it actually was.

Of course, Tuchel may still harbour those reservations about Alexander-Arnold's defending, and they were not put to the test here, but these few seconds showed exactly what he is about and what he can rightly argue is his unique selling point.

The defensive questions must wait for another day. The answers, whenever they come, would appear to shape Tuchel's thinking and Alexander-Arnold's England career, but he deserves the opportunity to provide them.

A delighted Tuchel told BBC Radio 5 Live: "He (Alexander-Arnold) did very well. He had an excellent assist. Overall, like everyone, he was professional, top attitude and one decisive action."

He added: "We never doubted that he can produce these kinds of assists. The deeper position in the second half suited him more than the higher position in the first half.

"Overall, I think we had a good and professional performance. Of course, the red card, especially an early red card, is such a heavy influence in the game. It makes the task sometimes a little bit more complicated psychologically."

Gordon, the grateful beneficiary of Alexander-Arnold's class, said: "I make that run time and time again and only a certain number of players have that ability, technique and bravery to be willing to make the mistake trying that pass. That's why he's so good and I've been dying to play with him for that reason.

"He's had his own journey with England. He would've liked to have played more than he has but he's been a great character during this camp. I've really enjoyed being around him."

Alexander-Arnold is a risk taker, both in the defensive and attacking context, but only Elliot Anderson (41) made more passes in the final third than he did (32), while only Anthony Gordon, with four, created more chances than the defender's three.

Tuchel, it should be stated, is not alone in having doubts about Alexander-Arnold.

Who can forget – although many would love to – Sir Gareth Southgate's ill-fated attempt to utilise Alexander-Arnold as a midfielder at Euro 2024? It was ditched after 54 minutes of England's second game against Denmark never to be seen again.

More will be revealed if Tuchel persists with Alexander-Arnold against Croatia behind closed doors in Rijeka on Saturday – but this must be close to make or break time for this lavishly-talented player who is 28 on 7 October.

If he cannot convince Tuchel in this camp, and surely that one moment of game-changing skill must be fixed in the head coach's mind, then you wonder if he ever will.

Alexander-Arnold said: "It was amazing. It's always an honour to represent my country. It's been a long time, but I've always believed I can play for England. That belief has always been there and it was about proving it at club level. The manager gave me a chance, now hopefully he is happy with how I played."

How happy? Time, and Tuchel, will tell.

Alexander-Arnold, however, could not have done any more as England, who sealed the three points with captain Harry Kane's 87th goal in 123 international appearances, got their Nations League campaign going in Prague.

title: Yamal inspires Spain to Croatia romp on World Cup homecoming
description:

Captain Rodri showed off the World Cup trophy before kick-off at the packed Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan, being handed it by Sevilla legend Jesus Navas, a winner with Spain in 2010.
fullText:
Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the World Cup.

Yamal, 19, was joined on the scoresheet by Marc Pubill and Nico Williams as they extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches, which includes June's final triumph over Argentina in the United States.

La Roja next play Czech Republic on Saturday in Group A3.

Yamal's contribution strengthened his case for the Ballon d'Or, with voting having closed on Monday and the winner announced on October 26.

Captain Rodri showed off the World Cup trophy before kick-off at the packed Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan, being handed it by Sevilla legend Jesus Navas, a winner with Spain in 2010.

"We were very excited to bring the cup here," Yamal said.

"To be able to win the game and bring it home is great," he added.

Attackers Yamal, Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal started the game having scored in Saturday's thrilling 3-2 win over England at Wembley.

Croatia made six changes from the weekend's win over the Czech Republic, leaving icon Luka Modric on the bench.

Yamal opened the scoring within two minutes against the Three Lions and took just 75 seconds to do so against Slaven Bilic's side in Andalusia.

The teenager's left-footed finish took his tally of international goals to nine in 36 appearances.

Just before the half-hour mark, the visitors equalised through Dion Beljo's header as the 1.95m-tall attacker headed home from an Ivan Perisic cross.

Two minutes later the hosts restored their lead as Pubill fired home a header from a pin-point Yamal cross.

Just 45 seconds before the interval, the home side were denied a third goal by the post as Fermin Lopez failed to find the bottom corner.

Yamal claimed his second after 63 minutes, beating Barcelona team-mate and Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic at his near post, and with fewer than two minutes to play Athletic Bilbao's Williams notched up a fourth for Spain with a crisp dribble and finish.

title: Fabian Ruiz unbeaten record: Spain midfielder holds improbable international streak without defeat
description: Spain and PSG midfielder Fabian Ruiz may not be the world's biggest superstar, but he has been one of the most successful international players in the history of the game so far.
fullText:
Fabian Ruiz unbeaten record: Spain midfielder holds improbable international streak without defeat originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

As the defending FIFA World Cup champions Spain begin the next four-year cycle in the hopes of defending their global title, one player has a personal streak on the line as well.

Spain and PSG midfielder Fabian Ruiz may not be the world's biggest superstar, but he has been one of the most successful international players in the history of the game so far.

The 30-year-old has never lost on the international level, a streak that is now over 50 games long. This has brought him untold success, having won a World Cup title, a European championship, and other trophies alongside.

The Sporting News brings you a breakdown of the improbable streak Fabian Ruiz is currently on and how it stands against others in the sport.

MORE:Timeline for Kylian Mbappe's injury return after being felled on France duty

With Fabian Ruiz on the field in some capacity, Spain have gone an incredible 52 games unbeaten in international competition.

Ruiz has never been on the field for a defeat at the international level.

Of note, the penalty defeat to Portugal in the 2024/25 UEFA Nations League final officially counts as a draw for team records, since the match itself played out to a 2-2 draw after extra-time, meaning a penalty shootout decided the match. A penalty shootout does not count as part of the official match when it comes to record-keeping.

Previously, the best unbeaten record in international football was owned by Jens Stryger Larsen, who went 36 games unbeaten to begin his international career before he suffered a 1-0 defeat to Finland in the group stage of Euro 2020 (which took place in June 2021).

It helps, of course, that Fabian Ruiz is playing for a Spain team on an international unbeaten streak of its own.

Spain have not suffered defeat for 40 straight competitive matches, dating back to a 2-0 loss to Scotland during Euro 2024 qualifying, which was just Luis de la Fuente's second game in charge of the side.

Since that loss, Spain have won the Euro 2024 title, lost the 2025 UEFA Nations League final on penalties, finished top of their World Cup qualifying group in unbeaten fashion, and won seven of eight matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup to lift the trophy.

Since Fabian Ruiz debuted internationally on June 7, 2019 against the Faroe Islands, here are the defeats Spain have suffered while he was absent from the team:

Ukraine 1-0 Spain (Oct. 13, 2020 — UEFA Nations League)

Sweden 2-1 Spain (Sep. 2, 2021 — World Cup qualifying)

France 2-1 Spain (Oct. 10, 2021 — UEFA Nations League final)

Spain 1-2 Switzerland (Sep. 24, 2022 — UEFA Nations League)

Japan 2-1 Spain (Dec. 1, 2022 — FIFA World Cup)

Scotland 2-0 Spain* (Mar. 28, 2023 — Euro qualifying)

Colombia 1-0 Spain* (Mar. 22, 2024 — International friendly)

* In squad but unused substitute

Thanks in large part to the aforementioned international streak, Fabian Ruiz has racked up quite a trophy count.

Alongside having won two Champions League titles on club duty with Paris Saint-Germain, Ruiz has also won some of the international game's biggest titles as well.

Additionally, Ruiz won a UEFA European U-21 championship with Spain as well, although that does not count as part of his first-team trophy collection.
